title: How to Stop Getting One-Shot in Path of Exile 2
summary: Why you die in one hit in Path of Exile 2 and how to fix it with layered defenses: resistance caps, armour, evasion, energy shield, block, ailment avoidance, and charms - not a single magic stat.
description: A troubleshooting guide for dying instantly in Path of Exile 2: the defense layers that actually keep you alive and how to build them.
prerequisites: A character in Acts or early endgame
Basic understanding of your life and resistance values
author: Exile2 Guides Editorial Team

items.title: The core mistake
body: Relying on a single defense. One-shot deaths happen because no single layer is enough - you need resistances, a real life or energy shield pool, some avoidance (evasion, block, spell suppression), and recovery (charms, flasks) working together.

items.title: First fix (always)
body: Cap your elemental resistances at 75% (fire, cold, lightning). Uncapped resistances are the most common cause of sudden deaths, especially in Act 3 and maps where monster damage jumps.

items.title: Chaos is different
body: Chaos resistance is a separate, harder-to-cap pool, and Chaos damage doubles against Energy Shield. If you are an ES build, Chaos is your biggest one-shot risk.

sections.title: Defense layers
sections.caption: No layer alone saves you. Build several at once.

cells.how: Reduces physical hit damage; better at high life
Separate pool; Chaos doubles vs ES
Turn physical into fire, then mitigate with fire res

sections.note: Cloak of Flames-style conversion lets you turn an unmitigated damage type (physical) into one you have capped (fire), which is a strong layered defense.

sections.title: Defense by game stage
sections.intro: What to prioritise changes as you progress. Pick your stage.

tabs.label: Act 1-3
paragraphs: Early game is about not falling behind on the basics.
bullets: Keep life on every gear slot you can.
Pick up resistance rolls from quest rewards (Cold, Lightning, Fire).
Use flasks actively - a dead flask is a dead character.

tabs.label: Endgame maps
bullets: Cap all three elemental resistances before pushing tier.
Add a second layer: armour, evasion, or block depending on your build.
Socket Chaos resistance where you can; ES builds especially.

tabs.label: Boss fights
paragraphs: Bosses hit far above trash damage.
bullets: Stack life or ES and have recovery ready (charms, flasks).
Use ailment avoidance for telegraphed ground effects.
Layer block or spell suppression for the biggest hits.

sections.title: Why do I keep dying?
sections.intro: Select how you are dying. The tool points to the missing layer.

options.label: One big hit from a boss

rules.title: Build a real pool and recovery
steps: Increase life or Energy Shield; a thin pool dies to any big hit.
Add block, spell suppression, or evasion as a second layer.
Keep charms and flasks ready for instant recovery during the fight.

rules.title: Address Chaos and ES weakness
steps: Chaos doubles against Energy Shield - socket Chaos resistance if you run ES.
For DoT deaths, add Chaos resistance and ailment avoidance.
Consider Cloak of Flames conversion for physical-heavy Chaos fights.

rules.title: Add ailment avoidance
steps: Ground effects apply ignites, shocks, and poisons - add ailment avoidance.
Use movement to leave telegraphed zones rather than tanking them.
Flask suffixes that remove ailments help enormously.

rules.title: Stack layers from the ground up
steps: Cap elemental resistances at 75% first - the highest-impact fix.
Add life/ES, then one avoidance layer (evasion, block, or suppression).
Finish with recovery (charms, flasks) and conversion tricks.

defaultResult.title: General survivability plan
steps: Cap elemental resistances, grow your life/ES pool, add one avoidance layer, and keep recovery ready.
Treat Chaos separately and protect ES builds from it.
Watch the referenced defense guide for a full visual breakdown of the layers.

entries.creator: Spud the King
entries.description: A practical breakdown of the defense layers in Path of Exile 2: resistances, armour, evasion, energy shield, block, ailment avoidance, and recovery.
entries.takeaway: Stack multiple defense layers - no single stat keeps you alive through bosses and maps.

items.question: Is 75% resistance enough by itself?
answer: It is the single most important layer, but no. A 75%-resisted hit can still one-shot a thin life pool. You still need a real pool and usually a second layer.

items.question: Why does Chaos hurt my Energy Shield build so much?
answer: Chaos damage doubles against Energy Shield, and Chaos resistance is harder to cap. ES builds should actively socket Chaos resistance or convert the incoming type.

items.question: Armour or Evasion - which is better?
answer: Neither is universally better. Armour mitigates physical hits and scales with high life; Evasion avoids hits and pairs with spell suppression. Pick based on your build and add the other as a secondary layer.
